findings.description: The calculation `(max + 1) * sizeof(int)` can overflow if `max` is close to `INT_MAX`.
Negative values in the input array will cause out-of-bounds memory access when used as array indices.
No checking if `malloc()` returns NULL (memory allocation failure).
If the array is empty (`n = 0`), accessing `arr[0]` causes undefined behavior.
Negative array values will cause writes to memory before the allocated buffer.
Very large positive values can cause integer overflow in memory allocation size calculation.
